artists.biography:
The Mission, known as The Mission UK in the United States, are an English gothic rock band formed in Leeds in 1986 by vocalist and guitarist Wayne Hussey and bassist Craig Adams, both former members of the Sisters of Mercy. The original lineup was completed by drummer Mick Brown of Red Lorry Yellow Lorry and guitarist Simon Hinkler. Emerging from the mid-1980s post-punk scene, the group developed a dramatic sound built on expansive guitar work, melodic bass lines, atmospheric keyboards, and Hussey’s distinctive, resonant vocals.

The band established its reputation with God’s Own Medicine (1986), followed by the influential albums Children (1988) and Carved in Sand (1990). Later releases including Masque, Neverland, Blue, Aura, God Is a Bullet, The Brightest Light, and Another Fall from Grace reflected their continuing evolution across gothic rock, darkwave, and darker alternative styles. Through lineup changes, breakups, reunions, and sustained touring, The Mission became one of the defining bands of British gothic rock, helping shape the genre’s grand, romantic, and emotionally charged sound.

perplexity.description:
Carved in Sand is The Mission’s third studio album, originally released in February 1990 and widely regarded as the band’s creative and commercial peak. Produced by Tim Palmer, it combines expansive gothic-rock atmospheres, ringing guitars, dramatic vocals, and sweeping melodic hooks across songs such as “Butterfly on a Wheel,” “Deliverance,” “Into the Blue,” and “Hands Across the Ocean.” The album reached No. 7 in the UK Albums Chart, while “Butterfly on a Wheel” became a major single, peaking at No. 12.

The 2026 Limited MMXXVI MWIS Edition, issued by Demon Records, is a collector-focused vinyl reissue rather than a new recording. It recreates the original gloss-laminated sleeve and printed inner, features new mastering by George Shilling, and is pressed on black/oxblood colour vinyl. Its ten-track program retains the album’s original sequence, from “Amelia” and “Into the Blue” through “Hungry as the Hunter” and “Lovely,” making the edition a carefully presented revival of a landmark late-1980s/early-1990s rock album.
